package-lock.json.summary: The locked dependency tree, generated by npm.

package.json.summary: The package manifest: scripts, dependencies, and the Node version this project needs.

public/babylon.d.ts.summary: The slice of the Babylon.js global the page uses, so the browser code type-checks without importing the library.

public/batch.ts.summary: Draws many copies of one shape in a single Babylon batch, tinted per slot for the file boxes and layer pads.

public/blocks.ts.summary: The blocks a source file is made of, the files and names each block imports, whether it is exported, and the rules that stack blocks into floors.

public/boxes.ts.summary: Draws and places every file box, batching the crowd and answering which box sits under the pointer.

public/chat.ts.summary: The built-in chat panel: the prompt box, the streaming conversation, and links from a reply to a file.

public/chatwire.ts.summary: The shapes of the chat event stream and state, shared by the page and the server.

public/city.ts.summary: Lays the repository's folder tree out as a treemap and feeds the shapes that draw it.

notes.restack: Re-heights the file boxes and layer planes when the spread slider moves the layer gap, without laying the treemap out again, so only a file's height changes. `snap` false moves only the resting heights, so leaving the concept view can glide back.

public/concepts.ts.summary: Zooms the map out from files to operations as columns, with the data they read and write as hexagons floating at their layers, and opens each operation as a process sheet.

notes.buildLayout: Places each operation in one of the two banks with a spine of shared data between them, docks the data only one operation touches beside its column, and gives every file a spot in its owning operation's column. Files no operation names gather under 'Not in an operation'.
notes.conceptTargets: Runs each frame after the route has set its targets, so while the zoom is on every file glides to its operation and shrinks to a dot; the size it had is kept so zooming back restores it.
notes.setZoom: Turns the zoom on or off: collapses the layer gap to its narrowest on the way in and restores the previous gap on the way out, puts away the city's ground, layer planes, labels, rings, and wires, frames the camera from above, and on the way back restores every file to its terrace.
notes.conceptTap: A tap in the concept view stays in it: a file opens its details and empty space puts the sheet away.
notes.openOperation: Clicking an operation's name zooms back in and shows its files lit in place, with the operation's summary as the note.
notes.declutter: Of the names shown, hides one that would cover a more important one (the chosen one and what it touches, then operations by size, then data).
notes.renderIndex: On desktop, lists every operation and data entry inside the right panel alongside the outliner; on a phone it stays folded above the tabs until opened. Hovering a row names it on the map, and filtered views show only what remains.
notes.frameChoice: On a phone, a data entry is framed together with its writers and readers.
notes.dataLabel: Names a hexagon with its layer and how many files it holds.
notes.applyActive: Lights a chosen entry's writers and readers and its links, fades the rest, and ghosts what the filters leave nothing of.
notes.renderData: The data sheet lists Comes from and Goes to, each operation with the steps that touch the entry's files.
notes.namedNow: At rest each shown operation wears a quiet stem badge and data stays unnamed; hovering or choosing an item expands its full name and names what it touches.
notes.conceptHover: Hovering in the concept view names the first operation column or hexagon the pointer's ray meets (the columns are pickable for this alone), or the operation of a file outside any column.
notes.placeLeaders: Draws each listed file's pointer from whichever edge of the sheet faces the dot, hiding lines scrolled outside the sheet body or when the sheet is hidden.
notes.conceptFiles: The files an operation names in its own list and its steps, or the files a data entry holds, so choosing either can bring them back into the scene.
notes.setActive: Chooses an operation or data entry: brings back any of its files an eye hid, opens its sheet in the right panel, and on a phone frames the chosen column or hexagon in the upper half.
notes.fitData: Places every data hexagon below the lowest file dot and puts the spine deck just under it, so data reads as the ground the operations stand on rather than as more files among them.

public/controls.ts.summary: The map's controls and options: framing the chosen block, file, or folder; colouring (choosing History opens its tab), grouping, filters (including picking out a layer from its legend name), shift-click selection, collapsing the outliner, and refreshing the graph.

notes.setupDockResize: Attaches width resize grips to the left dock's panels (including the tools bar) and the right dock (saved in localStorage), and height resize grips to the left-column foldable panels, with double-click reset.
notes.revealValue: Brings back the hidden files of a system or layer being switched on, so a chosen slice always draws something.
notes.toggleSlice: Turns one system or layer on or off; switching one on brings back its hidden files, then reaches the other strip's values it needs so the selection never locks them out.
notes.isolateSlice: Shows only one system or layer, or brings them all back when it is already alone; isolating a value brings back its hidden files.
notes.spotLayer: Picks a layer from the legend to keep bright while the rest fade in place; picking one brings back any of its files an eye hid.
notes.setLayerGap: Sets the layer gap from code and keeps the spread slider in step, without re-stacking the city, so the concept view can collapse and restore it.

public/edges.ts.summary: Draws import edges, tethers, route strands, a route's import graph, and block wires, landing an incoming wire on the exported block the importer names.

public/endpoint.ts.summary: Builds every address the page uses to reach the server, relative to the page and carrying its ?repo=.

public/filter.ts.summary: The pure filter and search rules the state and outliner share, kept testable away from the scene and DOM.

public/floors.ts.summary: Opens a chosen file box into its block stack in two stages, frames a chosen block's floor, picks the block under a tap, and exposes each floor's top so wires can meet the block by name.

public/flows.ts.summary: The saved-view shape and its limits, shared by the page and the server so a field rename cannot drift.

public/health.ts.summary: The health check's answer and its parts, shared by the page and the server so a field rename cannot drift.

public/highlight.ts.summary: Paints each file for the current choice, tinting the batched crowd, lighting every selected file, fading a file that was just edited, and greying the layers left out when one is picked from the legend.

public/history.ts.summary: The shape of a commit and the rule that turns the git history into a per-file heat, shared by the server that reads git and the page that colours the map.

notes.MaxHistoryCommits: How many of the newest commits the server reads, so a long history stays a small answer.
notes.HeatWindow: How many commits a touched file takes to cool from red back to blue.
notes.IHistoryCommit: One commit: its hash, date, subject, and the files it touched, named as they are today.
notes.buildTimeline: Reads the commits once into each file's list of touching commits and the commit it first appeared in.
notes.historyHeat: A file's heat at one commit: -1 before it existed, 1 when that commit touched it, fading to 0 over the heat window; a file git never saw exists only at the newest commit.

public/index.html.summary: The page's HTML shell: the canvas, the left-docked tools bar and detail panels, the right-docked concepts/outliner/chat tabs, the insights panel and its phone tab, and the bootstrap request for the repository.

public/ingest.ts.summary: The shape of the ingest-status response, shared by the page and the server.

public/insight.ts.summary: The Insights panel and its bottom-bar buttons: the files changed since HEAD, the saved flows with the start-here tour, the commit history scrubber, and the health check.

notes.renderHistory: Reads /api/history, switches the map to history colouring, and draws the commit bars, the scrubber and the play button.
notes.paintHistory: Updates the stats, the commit line and the bars for the commit the scrubber stands at, without redrawing the tab.
notes.goToCommit: Moves the scrubber to one commit and repaints the map.
notes.leaveHistory: Restores the colouring the map had before the tab opened, so history colouring never outlives its controls.

public/labels.ts.summary: Places names, tags, step captions, and the layer legend with its leader lines on screen without letting them pile up or overlap.

public/main.ts.summary: Boots the page: pointer interaction that picks files, folders, and floors, shift-click selection, the render loop with the edit flash, and the first load.

public/meshes.ts.summary: Builds, reuses, and retires each file's mesh so its box sits on its folder's tile and animates into place.

public/mobile.ts.summary: The phone layout: a bottom tab bar whose sheets hold the same panels rather than copies of them, with the insights panel in a sheet of its own.

public/neighbourhood.ts.summary: Narrows the map to one file and what it imports or is imported by, and chooses the file, from the server's neighbours endpoint.

public/neighbours.ts.summary: The depth rule and the neighbour shape, shared by the server that walks the graph and the page that asks for one.

public/pads.ts.summary: Draws a thin ring for each file on its own layer plane, in the layer's colour, so its layer reads at a glance.

public/panels.ts.summary: The outliner, the info panel with its block rail and start-here link, the neighbourhood action, and the selected files with their actions, and everything a person can click, select, fold, or search.

notes.renderFilterStrip: Draws one switch per system and layer with a live count. A value is selectable when it holds any file that passes the tag filter, even if an eye hid them all, since switching it on brings them back; only a value with no such file is empty.

public/repo-switch.ts.summary: The Repo panel: points the map at another folder, walks and lists recent repositories, reports how much is left to describe, refine, and design, and starts the ingest, refine, and delete actions.

notes.showPanel: Opens the repository switcher, refreshes ingest status, and skips folder browsing when the page is pinned by ?repo=.

public/repo.ts.summary: Loads the graph, source, blocks, and import names from the server, flashes edited files, and folds the folder tree into map nodes.

public/route.ts.summary: Lifts the files of a shown route into an ordered lane in front of the city and settles them back home.

public/rules.ts.summary: The map's pure folder, colour, layer-rank, visibility, ray-picking, and concept-spine layout rules, kept testable away from the scene.

notes.conceptFileOwners: Picks one column per file: the operation whose steps cite it most, the smaller on a tie, then gives any operation left empty a file back from the biggest column sharing it.
notes.conceptDataClaims: Picks the files that stand under a data entry's hexagon: each file it lists, unless an operation needs it to keep a column of its own.
notes.conceptTrace: For a data entry, the operations that write it (comes from) and read it (goes to), each with the step text that touches the entry's files.
notes.conceptFilterView: Which operations and data stay under the Outliner's filters: an operation with a drawn file, and data a remaining operation reads or writes.
notes.conceptFraming: The camera aim and distance that hold a set of points, never closer than the camera already is.
notes.conceptStems: Gives each operation a quiet one-word stem for its resting badge, adding a distinguishing word only when two operations open with the same verb.

public/shown.ts.summary: The shape of a map show request, shared by the page and the server.

public/state.ts.summary: The page's mutable world and constants: the graph, the chosen file and block, the selection, import names, filters, the layer picked from the legend, edit flashes, wire anchors, scene handles, the commit the history colouring stands at, and camera framing for a file's block stack or a chosen floor.

notes.frameFile: Glides the camera to a chosen file and its block stack; in the concept view it goes to the file's dot instead, and frameFolder does nothing there.
notes.revealFiles: Brings files back from an eye that hid them, so a chosen concept or filter slice always draws its files. A file's own eye wins over its folder's, so it opens the folders above the file without showing the rest.
notes.MIN_LAYER_GAP: The narrowest the spread slider allows, the gap the concept view collapses to.

public/style.css.summary: The styles for the page, the left and right docks, the tools and bottom control bars, the outliner and its edge tab, the block rail, the insights panel, and the phone sheets.

public/symbols.ts.summary: Reads the declarations a source file lists, with the lines they span, for search.

public/tags.ts.summary: The one ordered tag vocabulary and its colours, shared by the browser and the server.

public/types.ts.summary: The shapes the page shares between its modules: the folder tree, each file's live record, and a shown route.

public/view.ts.summary: The Showing panel and view events from the server or this page: shows a route and its import graph, selects and isolates files, frames the whole route or selection, and does not repeat a step's own summary.

notes.show: Lights the files a tool or this page asked for, brings back any an eye hid, and frames the whole route or set.

public/viewcall.ts.summary: Changes the view for the page's own buttons: through the server so every page follows, or in this page alone when a read-only host refuses the write.

src/agent/BlockSummaries.ts.summary: Writes one sentence for each block a file leaves without a comment, through the configured model, and keeps the answers for the session.

src/agent/Chat.ts.summary: Runs the built-in pi agent in the repository being mapped, streams its replies, and lists past chats.

src/agent/Instructions.ts.summary: The system prompt that tells the chat's agent about Codespace, the map's endpoints, and how to describe a repository.

src/agent/ModelSettings.ts.summary: Reads the chat's model endpoint and key from the environment, with sensible defaults.

src/cli/Cli.ts.summary: The commands an agent runs to describe a repository: what is left, the next batch, applying it, installing the upkeep rules, and the second pass.

notes.RunAsync: apply records the files it names and the files of each concepts entry it writes (RecordAppliedAsync).

src/cli/Options.ts.summary: Reads `--name value` or `--name=value` options from a command line.

src/repo/Architecture.ts.summary: Reads, validates, and writes a repository's architecture file and the batches applied to it.

notes.Architecture.ReadConcepts: Reads the optional concepts section: data by name, and operations with the files they live in and the data they read and write. A file that does not exist or a thing that is not declared is dropped with a warning.
notes.LegacyConcepts: Reads a file or patch written when data was called "things" as data, so older maps keep working.

src/repo/Blocks.ts.summary: Reads the blocks a file is made of, with a summary, their references, exported names, and the files their own text imports.

src/repo/Concepts.ts.summary: Hands out the concepts pass: every described file as a paged overview, then operations and data still missing fields, then the files nothing names, then entries whose files changed, then a review of what the design leaves.

notes.ReviewConcepts: Checks the design against the files and imports: systems with nothing placed, data no operation reads or writes, data holding more than 15 files, near-duplicate operations, unplaced imports, and writing issues.
notes.ConceptsNextAsync: Stages: overview, operations, data, place, changed, review, done. The changed stage hands back flagged entries with reason changed, the changed paths, and the current entry, and counts them in remaining.
notes.DesignFiles: Every file the design can name: all but the generated and vendored ones, so the agent judges tests, docs, and data tables itself.
notes.BuildOverview: Lists every design file with its system, layer, tags, summary, and import counts, cut into pages by size so nothing is trimmed.
notes.FilesToPlace: The described files the design must place: every one but the generated and vendored ones.
notes.DataMissing: A data entry is finished once it has a layer and names the files that define or hold it.
notes.ConceptsDriftAsync: Compares each operation's and data entry's stamped files with their text now; an entry with no stamps is never flagged.
notes.RecordAppliedAsync: Run after every apply: stamps the files the patch names, and the files each operation and data entry it writes names; removed entries lose their stamps.
notes.ConceptsLeft: Counts what the design still needs, plus (given the drift) how many operations and data entries changed.

src/repo/ConceptsGuide.ts.summary: The instructions an agent follows to write data and operations as process sheets, shared by the CLI and the chat.

src/repo/DescribeGuide.ts.summary: The first-pass instructions for describing a repository, shared by the copied prompt and the built-in chat.

src/repo/Flows.ts.summary: Reads and writes the flows a repository keeps at .codespace/flows.json, checks them against the files, and drafts a start-here tour from the descriptions.

src/repo/Graph.ts.summary: Reads the import graph between a repository's files, with the names each file takes from each imported file, and resolves one specifier to its file.

src/repo/Health.ts.summary: Describes the shape of a codebase and points at what is worth a look: its size, the files nobody described, the imports that go up the layers, the largest files, and values that look like keys.

src/repo/History.ts.summary: Reads the git history of the repository folder into commits with the files each touched, following renames to the name a file has now.

notes.ParseHistory: Splits the log into commits and walks them newest first, so a file touched before a rename is credited to its current path; deleted files are dropped.
notes.ReadHistoryAsync: Runs git log oldest first, relative to the repository folder, and returns no commits outside git or without git.

src/repo/Ingest.ts.summary: Chooses what an agent reads next to describe or update the codebase, and how large one batch may be.

src/repo/Install.ts.summary: Leaves the upkeep rules in the repository being mapped, so whoever changes it later keeps its architecture file true.

src/repo/JsonStore.ts.summary: The one guarded atomic store for the files Codespace keeps beside a repository, JSON or text, refusing any path that leaves it.

src/repo/Ledger.ts.summary: Remembers what each file, and each file an operation or data entry names, looked like when it was written, so a later pass can tell which descriptions and design entries have gone stale.

notes.Ledger.ReadConceptsAsync: The design stamps: for each operation and data entry, the hash of every file it named when it was applied. An entry with none was written before stamps existed and counts as current.
notes.Ledger.RecordConceptsAsync: Stamps the files an applied operation or data entry names, replacing that entry's earlier stamps.
notes.Ledger.ForgetConceptsAsync: Drops the stamps of removed entries.
notes.Ledger.HashesAsync: Hashes each named file once, so drift compares many entries without reading a file twice.
notes.Ledger.ReadAllAsync: Reads the whole ledger file: file stamps and design stamps.
notes.Ledger.ChangeAsync: Reads and rewrites the whole ledger under the lock, so a file-stamp change never drops the design stamps.

src/repo/LiftNotes.ts.summary: Moves the plain-English comments out of a repository's scripts into its architecture file as notes, so explanations live beside the map rather than in the code.

src/repo/Neighbours.ts.summary: Finds the files around one file: the chosen file, the files it imports, and the files that import it, outward by one step.

src/repo/Next.ts.summary: The one way to hand out the next files or folders to describe, shared by the CLI and the map API.

src/repo/Refine.ts.summary: Checks a repository's layers and systems against its imports and points at the breaks, misfits, and layering problems worth a second look.

src/repo/RefineGuide.ts.summary: The instructions for the second pass of describing a repository, shared by the copied prompt and the built-in chat.

src/repo/Repo.ts.summary: Reads a folder as a repository: lists and stamps its files, giving each its own stamp so an edited file can be told, and reads source safely, honoring gitignore and skipping vendored code.

src/repo/ShowLimits.ts.summary: The limits on one show request: how many files, and how long each note, the title, and the overall note may be.

src/repo/Snapshot.ts.summary: Reads everything the page needs to draw a repository in one pass, with each file's stamp and import names, and reuses it until a file changes.

src/repo/Sync.ts.summary: The housekeeping before an update: entries follow files that were moved, entries for deleted files are dropped, and older descriptions are stamped.

src/server/Api.ts.summary: The endpoints for the architecture, the import graph, a file's neighbours, the tool list, the view stream, flows, the health check, ingest status, next and refine, the selection, and the chat.

notes.Api.UpdateArchitectureAsync: Stamps files and design entries as the CLI's apply does; the status endpoint counts changed operations and data.

src/server/Guard.ts.summary: Decides whether a request may change anything, allowing writes from this machine or localhost unless told otherwise.

src/server/Server.ts.summary: Serves the page and its assets, the installed Babylon build, and the repository endpoints over HTTP, with stamps, import names, the workspace, and the view stream.

src/server/Tools.ts.summary: The one list of what an agent can do with the map, including its neighbours, history, health check, saved flows and tour, and the concepts pass, each as an HTTP call for hosts and the built-in chat.

src/server/View.ts.summary: Holds what the map is being asked to show, isolate, and select, and streams view and chat events to every open page.

src/server/Workspace.ts.summary: The repositories a server reads, each with its own view and a watch on its architecture file that tells the open pages to redraw.

tests/Api.test.ts.summary: Tests the HTTP endpoints over a small temporary repository, including the chat guard, show limits, and the view stream.

tests/Architecture.test.ts.summary: Tests reading, validating, and patching the architecture file.

tests/BlockSummaries.test.ts.summary: Tests writing block summaries through a stand-in model: the request it sends, the replies it reads, the session cache, and the missing key.

tests/Blocks.test.ts.summary: Tests reading a file's blocks, their summaries, references, exports, and imported files, and the floor stack they make.

tests/Chat.test.ts.summary: Tests the chat's transcript lines, model settings, instructions, and its busy, stop, and new-chat lifecycle.

tests/Cli.test.ts.summary: Tests the describe CLI's commands against temporary repositories, including size limits, generated files, malformed batches, the ledger, and next's move and delete housekeeping.

tests/Concepts.test.ts.summary: Checks the concepts pass: reading and merging the section, the staged hand-out, drift after a file changes, review, the layout, tracing and filtering.

tests/Filter.test.ts.summary: Tests the pure filter and search rules behind the map's outliner.

tests/Flows.test.ts.summary: Checks a flow is trimmed and checked, the tour begins at an entry and follows its imports, and the flows endpoints save, show, and delete.

tests/Graph.test.ts.summary: Tests the import graph between files, including the names each file takes from an import, for C# and TypeScript.

tests/Guard.test.ts.summary: Tests which requests may read or write through the server, and how request bodies are read.

tests/Health.test.ts.summary: Checks the health survey counts a codebase and names its largest files and layer breaks, and that the secret scan finds key-shaped values without returning them.

tests/History.test.ts.summary: Checks renames are followed and deletions dropped, the heat rule, and that a real checkout is read oldest first and served at /api/history.

tests/Ingest.test.ts.summary: Tests which files and folders the describe loop hands back, which are settled, and how long files are cut.

tests/Install.test.ts.summary: Checks the upkeep rules are written once, only inside their own marked block, and never through a link that leaves the repository.

tests/JsonStore.test.ts.summary: Tests the one write path: whole writes with no temporary file left, and a .codespace path that is a file being refused untouched.

tests/LiftNotes.test.ts.summary: Checks that lifting comments makes the right notes, leaves other comments, and that the blocks then read their summaries from the notes.

tests/Neighbours.test.ts.summary: Checks a neighbourhood walks imports both ways by one step, caps its size, and clamps the depth asked for.

tests/Pinned.test.ts.summary: Tests that ?repo= reads another repository beside the server's own, who may open one, and the server without its chat.

tests/Refine.test.ts.summary: Checks the second pass finds layer breaks, better layers, misplaced files, and layering problems, and stays quiet on a tidy repository.

tests/Repo.test.ts.summary: Tests listing a repository's files, refusing paths outside it, and always hiding the machine-local ledger.

tests/Rules.test.ts.summary: Tests the pure folder, colour, layer-rank, visibility, and ray-and-box rules the map shares.

tests/Server.test.ts.summary: Tests serving the page and assets, the bootstrap with stamps and import names, repository switching, changes (including a folder inside a larger checkout), and the view stream.

tests/Snapshot.test.ts.summary: Tests reading a snapshot once and reusing it, each file's stamp, the names it imports, and narrowing import edges to a folder.

tests/Symbols.test.ts.summary: Tests reading the declarations a source file lists, and which files count as code.

tests/Tools.test.ts.summary: Tests that the tool list is well formed, is served, reaches the chat, and that every listed tool, including flows and health, answers through the real server.

tests/Update.test.ts.summary: Checks an update hands back only what changed, catches equal-size edits, carries entries along with moved files, and drops those for deleted ones.

tests/Workspace.test.ts.summary: Tests opening, switching, and listing recent repositories, and resolving typed paths.

tests/support.ts.summary: Shared helpers that make temporary repositories and start the API or server over them.

tsconfig.json.summary: The TypeScript settings for the server side and tests.

tsconfig.web.json.summary: The TypeScript settings for the browser code in public/, which compiles beside its source.

.codespace.summary: The map's own description of this repository: the architecture file it reads.

docs.summary: Documentation for the map: the architecture-file guide, the glossary, the review rubric, and deferred ideas.

public.summary: The browser side: the Babylon city, the panels and chat around it, and the state they share.

src.summary: The Node side: reading repositories, serving the map, the describe CLI, and the built-in chat.

src/agent.summary: The built-in chat: its pi agent, what that agent is told, and which model it uses.

src/cli.summary: The commands an agent runs to describe a repository and write its architecture file.

src/repo.summary: Reads a repository: its files, its architecture file, its import graph, and what to ingest next.

src/server.summary: The HTTP server, its endpoints, the view stream, the write guard, and the switchable workspace.

tests.summary: Tests for the server side, plus the dependency-free browser helpers.

Your folder.summary: The repository on disk: its text files, as the map is allowed to read them.
rules: Files the repository ignores, and anything a link points outside the folder, are never read.

Snapshot.summary: Every readable file with its stamp, line count, declared names, and imports, read in one pass and reused until a file changes.
rules: A failed read is never remembered, so the next request reads again.

Architecture file.summary: What each file is for, the layers and systems it sits in, and the things and operations of the design, kept beside the repository.
rules: A change is all or nothing: one problem refuses the whole change and writes nothing.
A system, layer, or thing must be declared before anything uses it, and one still in use cannot be removed.
Every summary and note is at most 2000 characters.
It is written whole, so a reader never sees half of it, and only inside the repository.

View.summary: What every open page is showing: a lit set, a route, an isolation, or a selection.
rules: A new show replaces the last show, a new isolation the last isolation, and a new selection the last selection.
Clearing takes down the show but leaves an isolation in place.

Flows.summary: Saved walks through the code, kept with the repository.
rules: A flow's paths are checked against the repository whenever it is saved or shown.
A repository keeps at most 50 flows.

Description record.summary: What each described file looked like when its entry was written, so a later edit shows up as changed.
rules: It stays on this machine and is not committed.

Chat transcript.summary: The conversation with the built-in agent, kept for each repository so it can be reopened.
rules: The chat reads only the server's own repository, never one opened with a repo address.

Drawn map.summary: The 3D city on the page: a box per file, layer pads, import wires, and the lit set.

Read a repository.summary: Turns a folder into the snapshot every other operation reads.

steps.text: List the readable text files, leaving out ignored folders and anything outside the repository.
Give every file a stamp from its size and time, and join them into one fingerprint for the whole repository.
Read each code file to count its lines and find the names it declares.
Work out which files import which, and which names each takes from the others.
Keep the result and hand back the same one until the fingerprint changes.

rules: The snapshot is rebuilt only when the fingerprint changes.

Describe files.summary: An agent reads the code in batches and writes each file's summary, system, layer, and tags into the architecture file.

steps.text: Move entries along with files that were moved, and drop the entries of files that are gone.
Settle generated and vendored files with a fixed summary, so nobody reads them.
Pick the next files that are new, changed since they were described, or missing a field, and hand them over with their text and imports.
The agent reads each file and writes its summary, system, layer, and tags, folders last.
Check the whole batch against the repository, then write it or refuse all of it with the reasons.
Remember what each described file looked like, so a later edit offers it again.
Leave the upkeep rules in the repository, so whoever changes it later keeps the file true.
Move explanations written as code comments into the file's notes.

rules: A file counts as described only with a summary, a system, a layer, and tags; generated files need only a summary.
Run again after changes: only what is new, changed, or incomplete is handed back.

Refine layers.summary: Checks the layers and systems against the imports so the picture of the stack is honest.

steps.text: Collect imports that point from a lower layer up to a higher one, grouped by pair of layers.
Find files that would sit in fewer breaks on another layer, and files whose neighbours are mostly in another system.
Flag layers and systems that look wrong as a whole.
The agent reads the files named, judges each break, and applies new layers, systems, or moves.

Chat.summary: The built-in agent answers questions and drives the map and the describe commands.

steps.text: Open an agent session in the repository, told what the map offers and how to describe code.
Send the person's message and stream the reply and each tool use to every open page.
The agent calls the map's endpoints and the describe commands to show code or write descriptions.
Keep each chat for the repository so it can be reopened.

rules: Only this machine may read or change the chat, and a page opened with a repo address has none.

Show on the map.summary: Lights up, isolates, selects, or frames files on every open page, as a route or a set.

steps.text: Accept the request only from this machine, unless the server allows writes from anywhere.
Keep the paths that are real files and report the rest as unknown.
Store the new view in place of the last of its kind and send it to every open page.
Each page lights the files, lifts a route into a lane, draws its wires, or narrows the map.

rules: At most 1000 files, and each note and title within a fixed length, are accepted in one show.

Open a repository.summary: Points the map at another folder and makes every open page follow.

steps.text: Accept the request only from this machine, unless the server allows writes from anywhere.
Resolve the chosen folder to its real path and check that it is a folder.
Forget what was shown and isolated, and start watching the new folder's architecture file.
Tell every open page to reload, and list the recent repositories in the Repo panel.

rules: A page opened on one repository with a repo address cannot switch to another.

Describe concepts.summary: An agent writes down the design as data and operations, for the person to confirm.

steps.text: Hand out every described file with its system, layer, summary, and import counts, page by page, with nothing picked out.
The agent reads the files, finds where work starts, and proposes data, the files that hold it, and operations with their steps, inputs, and outputs.
Hand back operations still missing steps, step files, or inputs and outputs (with nearby imports), and data missing a layer or files.
Review the design for files nothing names, uncovered systems, orphan data, overlaps, and unplaced imports.
Check every named data entry, file, and layer, then write the batch or refuse all of it.

rules: A thing that an operation still reads or writes cannot be removed.

Keep flows.summary: Saves named walks through the code with the repository, and drafts a start-here tour from the descriptions.

steps.text: Trim a flow's name and notes and check its paths against the repository.
Save it by name in the repository's flows file, replacing one of the same name, or delete it.
Draft a tour that starts at the entry files, then follows what they import, one step per file with its summary.
Show a saved flow by sending it to the view.

Report on the codebase.summary: Answers what is large, undescribed, recently changed, or tangled, and what surrounds one file.

steps.text: Count the files and lines, the files nobody described, the largest files, and the imports that go up the layers.
Scan the files a browser can read for values that look like keys.
List the files changed since the last commit with their line counts.
Read the last commits and the files each touched, following renames, and colour the map by them.
Walk the imports one or two steps around a file in both directions.
Show the answers in the Insights panel.

rules: The report decides nothing: the key scan is a pattern, not proof.

Explain a file.summary: Opens a file into its blocks, each with a sentence on what it is for.

steps.text: Read the file's text and split it into declarations and groups, with their line ranges and what they refer to.
Give each block the note written for it in the architecture file, else its own comment, else a plain description of its shape.
For blocks left with none, ask the configured model for one sentence and keep it for the session.
Stack the blocks into floors on the file's box and list them in the rail.

Draw the map.summary: Turns the snapshot and the architecture file into the 3D city, and redraws it when they change.

steps.text: Ask the server for the whole repository in one answer, and skip the rest if its fingerprint is unchanged.
Fold the folder tree into nodes and lay them out as a treemap.
Build or reuse a box for each file on its folder's tile, and a ring on its layer's plane.
Colour and filter the files by tag, system, layer, or history.
Draw the imports between files as wires, and label what is on screen.
Redraw when the server says the architecture changed, or when a poll finds a new fingerprint.
